sources.entry: Harness Open Source | Code hosting, CI/CD pipelines and artifact registry (formerly Drone CI and Gitness)

summary.one_liner: Harness Open Source is a self-hostable development platform combining code hosting, CI/CD pipelines, Gitspaces developer environments, and artifact registries, developed as the successor to Drone.
summary.what_it_does: Harness is an open source DevOps platform that bundles source code hosting, automated pipelines, hosted development environments called Gitspaces, and artifact registries. It ships as a Docker image that runs a server on port 3000 with a web UI and a swagger-documented REST API. Pipelines run inside Docker containers, and the README says the app negotiates the Docker API version with the local daemon. The project was built from the Drone CI codebase, which is kept as a separate feature branch, and development continues on main. Access is via a web UI, REST API with personal access tokens, and a basic CLI named gitness.
use_cases: migrate from Drone CI to a broader platform
how_to_run: Open the web UI in a browser on port 3000 once the container is up
Build from source: install Node and Go 1.20+, then run make dep and make tools
Build the UI: cd web && yarn install && yarn build, then run make build
notable: Successor to Drone CI, with Drone preserved as a feature branch while Harness reaches pipeline parity
Combines code hosting, pipelines, Gitspaces and artifact registries in one platform
Auto-negotiates Docker API version and documents socket setup for Docker Desktop, Rancher Desktop, and Colima
Generates a personal access token from the CLI for REST API use
caveats: Pipeline parity with Drone is a stated long-term goal, not yet reached
Data persists only if a bind mount or named volume is used; the README warns of data loss otherwise
The CLI is described as very basic
Some registry swagger endpoints are on a separate location and are planned to move
